variable_coverage.construction: Core RNOA_(t+1) = core operating income_(t+1) × (1 − statutory federal rate_(t+1) − 0.02) / average NOA_(t+1). The paper defines the verbal numerator and rate increment but does not specify the Compustat numerator field, statutory bracket/year mapping, or average-NOA interval; these remain unresolved.

Core RNOA_t = core operating income_t × (1 − statutory federal rate_t − 0.02) / average NOA_t. Source-supported years are scoring t=1976–1996; numerator-field mapping and the average-NOA window remain unresolved.

Q_t = 0.5(C_t − C_(t−1)) + 0.5(C_t − same-year two-digit-SIC median C_t), where C=(LIFO reserve + R&D reserve + advertising reserve)/NOA. NOA fields, LIFR, XRD, XAD, and historical SIC are mapped by catalog labels. R&D reserve uses cited Lev–Sougiannis industry coefficients, but their target-SIC crosswalk and pre-1975 initialization are unresolved; non-LIFO zero versus missing-reserve classification is also unresolved.

design_coverage.reason: No separate fixed-effect dimension is reported. The 21 calendar-year cross-sections are separate fits, not a pooled year-fixed-effect regression.
The Table 3 note does not report a cluster dimension or identify a per-year standard-error estimator.
No weights are reported for the selected Table 3 Panel A fits.
The source specifies 21 annual cross-sectional linear regressions and reports means and quartiles of their coefficients; the per-year estimator and standard-error method are not identified.

implementation_issues.description: The paper divides by average NOA but does not state whether this is a two-point, multi-year, or other average. The exact raw denominator dates and construction are therefore not bounded.

Core operating income is defined verbally as income before interest, special items, extraordinary items, and discontinued operations, but the target does not identify a Compustat item. OIADP/OIBDP are candidate current fields, not verified mappings.

The paper says statutory rate is Federal rate plus two percentage points. It does not identify which annual bracket/rate to use or how to align the calendar-year IRS schedule to firms’ fiscal-year RNOA observations.

Table 3 does not identify the estimator for each annual linear regression or the per-year standard-error estimator. It describes the t-statistic using the mean coefficient and estimated standard errors but leaves the calculation convention incomplete.
The article specifies two-digit-SIC industry medians and subscore substitutions but does not state the exact benchmark peer universe or which firms enter each component median.

The article identifies NYSE/AMEX nonfinancial firms and cites Compustat and 1997 CRSP data, but does not specify the exchange-code source, date-valid match, or exact nonfinancial SIC screen for this annual regression cohort.

Non-LIFO firms receive a zero inventory reserve, but the paper does not identify a current raw method flag or missing-versus-zero rule. A missing LIFR observation cannot be assumed to be a non-LIFO zero.

R&D reserve uses Lev–Sougiannis industry coefficients. Their cited schedule spans five to nine-year R&D lives, but the target does not state how to map its two-digit-SIC groups to that schedule or whether it uses pre-1975 R&D history/initializes capital stocks at 1975. The temporal window uses the nine-year maximum conservatively.
The paper used 1997 Compustat/CRSP data vintages. The available local annual Compustat and current public IRS schedule are later vintages; no local population coverage confirmation is supplied.

The Q score combines the current C score with the prior-year C score and the same-year two-digit-SIC industry median; the two components receive equal weight.
Section IV reports the final Q-score sample and the NYSE/AMEX nonfinancial Compustat Annual Industrial and Research source, including nonsurvivors, for 1975–1997.
Section V defines after-tax core RNOA, states the Federal rate plus two percentage points, and divides by average NOA; it does not specify the averaging interval.
Section V says the outcome is one-year-ahead core RNOA and the regressors are current-year core RNOA and Q score; the scoring years are 1976–1996.
Table 3 summarizes mean and quartile coefficients across 21 annual cross-sections; its note describes t-statistics but does not identify the underlying regression or standard-error estimator.

review_notes: The assigned baseline is Table 3 Panel A only: one fit family summarized across 21 annual cross-sections, scoring years 1976–1996. The reported mean and coefficient quartiles are summaries of those fits, not additional models.

The paper’s original sample data section names combined Compustat Annual Industrial and Research files with nonsurvivors and monthly returns from the 1997 CRSP files for 1975–1997. The selected Panel A regression uses accounting outcomes and predictors; CRSP returns are not themselves a frozen regression variable. Exchange-screen source/code matching remains unresolved.

Q_t requires C_t and C_(t−1). For advertising, the nested 12-month prior-C lag and the two-year sum-of-years-digits reserve produce raw XAD years 1974–1996. For R&D, Lev–Sougiannis’ maximum nine-year lag plus the one-year prior-C-score lag produces XRD years 1966–1996; the target does not state whether it uses pre-1975 inputs or how it maps its SIC groups to the referenced schedule.
Current Compustat and IRS sources are later public/local vintages than the paper’s 1997-data design. Current field labels support candidate mappings, but local population coverage is not confirmed.
